flagged.evidence: The Definition declares “η∈T_X St(n,r)” and then says “For Grassmann transport specifically choose Y=R_X^{pol}(η),” without requiring η to be horizontal in that branch. This matters: take X=[e₁ e₂] in ℝ³ˣ², H=[e₃ 0], and V=X[[0,-1],[1,0]]. H is horizontal and V is vertical, so H and H+V represent the same Grassmann tangent, but their polar endpoints have ranges span{e₁+e₃,e₂} and span{e₁+e₂+e₃,e₂−e₁}, respectively. These planes differ (e₂ is not in the second). Polar normalization preserves the input column space, so the endpoint depends on the lift. The Grassmann branch must specify the unique horizontal representative.
